decision: Feature 3 events: Mars–Jupiter conjunction (lead), Leonids peak, Moon–Saturn pass
rationale: Conjunction is the strongest visual hook (1.19°, both planets bright, 46° up in a dark pre-dawn sky). Leonids are modest (ZHR 15) but the Moon sets 23:28 so post-midnight skies are dark — worth a beat. Moon–Saturn is easy for casual viewers in the evening. Three events keeps it under 55 s.
alternatives: Mercury greatest elongation (rejected: only 8° up at its best moment — too low for a general audience)
Venus visibility (rejected: no news, low in dawn twilight)
First Quarter Moon (rejected: not an event)

decision: Insight beat: 3D orbit reveal — from Earth they line up, from above Mars is 195M km and Jupiter ~4x farther
rationale: Turns a 'two dots' event into a reason to share; uses computed distances (fact conj-…-dist). A NASA image of Jupiter was considered but adds no understanding.
alternatives: NASA Juno image of Jupiter (rejected: pretty but not explanatory)
Fact card '4x farther' (rejected: weaker than showing it)

decision: Reworded Leonids beat: 'peaks on Tuesday the 17th; look after midnight on the nights around the peak' (was 'on the night of the 17th')
rationale: Computed peak is Tue 17 Nov 15:52 local (daytime), roughly equidistant from the 16–17 and 17–18 observing windows, so naming one night overstated precision. Moonset fact (23:28) is for the 17th; the Moon also sets before midnight on the 16th, so 'before midnight' holds for both nights.

decision: Hide compass letters inside the caption band (renderer fix) and re-aim the outro camera to az 215°/alt 32° so the Moon leaves the CTA area
rationale: QA review found text collisions; fixing the renderer prevents the same issue in every future episode rather than tuning each plan.

decision: Outro footnote moved above the caption band (template fix); outro camera ends at az 262° so the Moon is off-frame
rationale: Second QA pass found the footnote colliding with captions and the Moon still under the CTA; template-level fix prevents recurrence.
